question: What is the main problem in diabetes mellitus?

options.C: High blood sugar that stays up

explanation: Diabetes mellitus happens when blood glucose levels remain high because the body has trouble making or using insulin properly. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which part of the body makes the hormone insulin?
explanation: Special cells inside the pancreas called the islets of Langerhans produce and release insulin into the body. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h1)

question: What is the main cause of Type 1 diabetes?

options.C: Body attacks its own insulin-making cells

explanation: Type 1 diabetes happens when the immune system mistakenly destroys the insulin-producing cells in the pancreas, stopping insulin production completely. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h2)

question: How is Type 2 diabetes different from Type 1?

options.A: The body resists insulin and doesn't make enough
options.B: The body stops making any insulin at all
options.C: It only happens in young children
options.D: It needs lifelong daily insulin from day one

explanation: In Type 2 diabetes, the body still makes some insulin, but the cells do not respond to it well, and the pancreas cannot keep up with the demand. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is the liver process of making new glucose from fats or proteins called?
explanation: Gluconeogenesis is how the liver creates fresh glucose from non-carbohydrate sources when the body needs energy. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why do ketone bodies form when diabetes is not controlled?

options.B: Cells lack glucose, so the body burns fat instead
options.C: The kidneys filter too much water
options.D: The kidneys turn extra blood sugar into ketones

explanation: When body cells cannot get glucose for energy, they break down stored fat instead, which leaves behind waste products called ketones. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h3)

question: What is the medical term for extreme thirst in diabetes?
explanation: Polydipsia means having an abnormally high level of thirst, which happens because the body is losing too much fluid. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why does high blood sugar cause frequent urination?

options.B: Extra sugar pulls water into the urine
options.C: High blood pressure pushes fluid directly to the bladder

explanation: High amounts of glucose act like a magnet, drawing water along with it into the urine and causing frequent trips to the bathroom. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h4)

question: How long does an HbA1c test show blood sugar control?
explanation: HbA1c measures sugar stuck to red blood cells, reflecting the average blood sugar over their 120-day lifespan. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h5)

question: What fasting blood sugar level points to a diagnosis of diabetes?
explanation: A fasting blood glucose reading of 7.0 mmol/L or higher on more than one test is a key diagnostic marker for diabetes. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h5)

question: What is the usual first drug given for Type 2 diabetes?
explanation: Metformin is the standard first medication because it helps lower liver sugar production and makes body cells more sensitive to insulin. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h6)

question: How does metformin help lower blood sugar?

options.B: By blocking water in the kidneys
options.C: By passing out extra protein in urine
options.D: By reducing liver sugar output and improving insulin use

explanation: Metformin works mainly in the liver to slow down glucose production while helping body tissues use insulin more effectively. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h6)

question: Which diabetic emergency involves high blood sugar, dehydration, and acid buildup?
explanation: Diabetic ketoacidosis happens when a severe lack of insulin causes high blood sugar, dehydration, and dangerous acid buildup from ketones. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h7)

question: What is the main difference between microvascular and macrovascular complications?

options.A: Macro has nothing to do with blood sugar
options.B: Macro happens faster in Type 1 diabetes
options.C: Micro affects small blood vessels, macro affects large ones
options.D: Micro affects the brain, macro affects limbs

explanation: The names come from the size of the blood vessels involved, with microvascular affecting tiny vessels in eyes and kidneys, and macrovascular affecting large arteries. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h7)

question: What daily foot care habit should a nurse teach a diabetic patient?

options.A: Soak feet in hot water every night
options.B: Check feet daily and keep them clean
options.C: Put strong medicated ointment between toes
options.D: Walk barefoot inside to make skin tough

explanation: Checking the feet every day helps spot small cuts or blisters early before they turn into hard-to-heal ulcers. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h8)

question: Why must nurses teach patients how to spot low blood sugar?

options.A: To stop them from drinking fluids
options.B: Low blood sugar can quickly cause confusion or fainting
options.C: To help them take more pills

explanation: Hypoglycemia is an urgent situation that needs quick action because dropping blood sugar can rapidly lead to confusion, seizures, or loss of consciousness. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h8)
